chapter: Other bands, mutes, arrangers and composers
title: Song pluggers, an Irving Berlin man at the Cave and war bonds
summary: DeDroit describes song pluggers paying bandleaders to play their songs, a Berlin representative at the Cave, and a patron's war bonds.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: This place for a while was a very lively place as far as music was. And composers, song pluggers, they all had agents here. You know? The first that they have an agent, and he'd come plugging, you know? They'd come on the bandstand and plug your tunes and if they had money, they'd pay you to pay them. I remember one fellow from Urban Berlin in the cave there. We played so many of his tunes that he said, Johnny, I like the way you play my tunes, but I don't have any more money. Because every time I played it, it was a 10 spot. We used to play maybe six sets at the most. I mean, it was $150. People. But it was $12 cover charge on that. I didn't even know you. $12 cover charge?
That was a long time ago, too.
During the war, one man came up and gave the whole band war bonds. This was the first World War? Yeah.
I gave him a stick, he led the band, he was beating it all around.
